rationale.automation-bias: Expected review increases capable humans’ deference to AI-generated output.
rationale.oversight-theater: Outcome-only review lacks process information and paradoxically weakens meaningful oversight.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Showing original and final outputs improves reviewers’ visibility into AI reliance.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Recommends retaining and submitting AI interaction logs for human review.
rationale.counterpoint: Challenges the prevailing assumption that review improves accountability and engagement.
rationale.general-ai: Studies AI-generated knowledge-work content rather than code specifically.
rationale.agentic: Participants receive complete posts, postcards, or lesson plans for gated submission.
rationale.non-developer: Participants are students, panelists, and teachers rather than professional developers.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Experiments measure passive acceptance and minimal modification of AI output.
rationale.method-experiment: Seven controlled experiments manipulate review and process-transparency conditions.
